newsitem.title: USA: PathoGenesis plans to file tobramycin NDA.
newsitem.headline: PathoGenesis plans to file tobramycin NDA.

text.p: PathoGenesis Corp said on Thursday it completed Phase III clinical trials of its treatment for chronic lung infections in people with cystic fibrosis and it planned to file a new drug application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the second quarter.

The company said TOBI, or tobramycin for inhalation, improved lung function in the two trials. Lung function improved by more than 11 percent by the end of the six month study period, the company said.
TOBI is a stable, premixed proprietary formulation of the antibiotic tobramycin for delivery by inhalation, it said.

The company conducted two double-blind, placebo controlled Phase III trials of its TOBI drug. A total of 468 patients in 69 cystic fibrosis care centers in the United States completed the trials, its said.
The mean number of hospitalization days across both studies declined 36 percent to 5.2 days for the TOBI group versus 8.2 days for the placebo group, it said.
The bacteria count observed in the phlegm of patients taking TOBI declined, while the bacteria count observed increased in the placebo group, it said.
